Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Chen, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Alex Rivera, CFO; Mike Thornton, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 was a significant quarter for Voltara Motors, marked by progress across our key strategic initiatives. We achieved notable milestones in record vehicle deliveries, explosive growth in software and services revenue, sharp declines in battery costs per kWh, aggressive factory expansions with efficiency gains, and a clear strategic outlook positioning us for accelerated growth. We also hit key achievements in overall performance that solidify our leadership in the premium EV space. We are particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our CyberVolt pickup, and its ramp-up has driven a substantial increase in our backlog to over 250,000 units.

These results reflect our relentless execution in a competitive landscape, where we're not just building vehicles but transforming into a tech platform company powered by software, autonomy, and scalable manufacturing. Before I hand over to Alex for the financial details, let me touch on our priorities looking ahead. We're guiding for continued momentum into Q4 and 2025, with aggressive production ramps targeting 310,000 to 330,000 deliveries this quarter alone. Our North Star is delivering vehicles with unmatched range, performance, and software ecosystems while capturing the 25% CAGR in global EV sales through 2028. Key focuses include ramping CyberVolt and our next-gen platforms, launching OTA updates for Level 3 autonomy via our neural networks trained on billions of miles of data, and expanding regionally—North America for IRA incentives, Europe to leverage tariffs on Chinese imports, and China with localized production. Capex will peak to support new Gigafactories, but we're on track for FCF positivity and EPS growth. Risks like interest rates and supply chains are real, but our vertical integration and hedging position us strongly.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. For Q3, our revenue reached $14.5 billion, demonstrating a 45% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin stood at 25%, reflecting our commitment to operational excellence through cost discipline and mix shifts. Operating expenses amounted to $3.2 billion, and net income was $1.1 billion. We maintain a robust financial position with $10.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for the upcoming quarter is revenue of $16-17 billion, with gross margins expanding to 26-27%.

As we unpack these results, let me highlight our overall company performance and key achievements, which underscore our position as the fastest-growing premium EV maker amid macroeconomic headwinds. We delivered 285,247 vehicles globally—a record, up 28% year-over-year from 222,619 and 15% sequentially from Q2's 248,102. This brings trailing 12-month deliveries to over 1 million units, driven by higher volumes, a stable ASP around $50,800, and software contributions. Gross profit hit $3.625 billion, with 450 basis points of expansion from efficiencies at our Nevada and Shanghai Gigafactories. Adjusted EBITDA reached $2.1 billion, or 14.5% of revenue—our strongest yet—and operating cash flow was $1.8 billion despite $1.1 billion in capex. Balance sheet remains fortress-like at $10.2 billion liquidity, funding expansions while we repurchased $300 million in shares. Production utilization hit 93%, with gigacasting slashing COGS 17% to $28,500 per unit. Our V3/Y models dominated at 77% mix, CyberVolt surged 450% YoY to 16%, and regionals balanced with North America at 42%, China 36%, Europe 17%. Software ARR per vehicle now exceeds $120, and backlog sits at 250,000 with quick fulfillment.

Diving deeper into one of our fastest-growing, highest-margin streams: software and services, including FSD subscriptions, infotainment, OTA upgrades, and robotaxi pilots. This generated $1.2 billion this quarter—up 185% YoY and 42% QoQ—now 18% of automotive revenue, up from 7% last year, heading to 25% by year-end as our connected fleet tops 2.5 million. Recurring subscriptions, our core, hit $850 million or 71% of the segment, via Voltara One tiers from $99/month for Enhanced Autopilot to $199 for FSD Supervised. ARPU rose 12% to $145/month, with 1.8 million paid subs globally, adding 450,000 net—34% YoY growth. Attachment rates on new V3/V4 deliveries reached 62%, boosted 28% by ML upselling on 15 billion fleet miles. Gross margins here shine at 92%, thanks to zero-marginal-cost OTA over our 5G-V2X network. Autonomous driving added $250 million, doubling YoY, from $8,000 FSD unlocks and beta fees, activating on 75% of 1.2 million eligible vehicles post-approvals in California, Texas, EU, and China via Baidu. FSD v12.3, our end-to-end neural net trained on expanded Dojo with 50,000 H100s from NVIDIA, cut urban interventions 45%; geo-fenced Level 4 pilots in Austin/Shanghai logged 2.5 million paid miles at $1.20/mile, 85% margins. Scaling to 10,000 robotaxis by mid-2025 could yield $2-3 billion annually. Other services like SuperVolt charging ($12/month unlimited) hit $100 million with 1 million subs, network at 15,000 stalls with 350kW chargers. North America led at 55%, Europe 25%, China 15% with 220% growth. This stream delivers 4x gross profit per vehicle vs. hardware, moated by in-house chips at 50 TOPS and 99.9% OTA rates; B2B licensing eyed for $500 million in 2025. Q3 guide: $1.6-1.8 billion, 50% YoY growth.

Another critical lever: battery costs per kWh, now at $92/kWh for NMC 811 packs in our premium models—lowest ever, down 18% YoY from $112, ahead of global $105 average. LFP for compacts at $78/kWh. Cumulative decline of 19% CAGR since 2020's $152, accelerating via scale at 250 GWh capacity, 95% yields on 4680 cells, in-house cathodes saving 25% logistics. Chemistry: 40% LFP mix stable at $70-80/kWh dodging nickel volatility; LMFP at $72/kWh with better life. Manufacturing: dry coating on 80% lines cuts capex 30%, cell-to-pack drops 15-20% weight, direct recycling saves $5-7/kWh. China leads at $65-75, but IRA narrows gap; Europe targeting sub-$85. Forecast: $72 by 2025, $58 by 2027 via solid-state pilots at 400 Wh/kg. This flywheel unlocks 20%+ margins.

On deliveries specifics: Model V3/Y at 220,450 (77%, +32% YoY), S/X 18,920 (7%), CyberVolt 45,877 (16%, +450%). North America 120,450 (+35%), China 102,300 (+25%), Europe 48,200 (+18%), APAC 14,297 (+42%). Inventory at 8 days, EV penetration 22%.

These metrics position us for outperformance. Next, I'll hand the call over to Mike Thornton for an update on our manufacturing operations.

Mike Thornton:
Thank you, Alex. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet the growing demand for our vehicles. We've implemented lean principles across the board, boosting throughput and cutting lead times significantly.

Specifically, factory expansions drove this: $4.2 billion capex, 60% to new sites like Phase 1 Texas Gigafactory—2.5 million sq ft, 400,000 units capacity for ED-7/ED-X on 800V, $2.1 billion invested. Europe Brandenburg to 250,000 units/$850 million upgrade for Battery Reg compliance, 95% regional content. Shanghai brownfield +150,000 to 650,000 total. Global capacity to 2.8 million, +45% YoY.

Efficiency gains via Smart Factory 2.0: 5,000 cobots, AI maintenance slashed downtime 35%, OEE to 93%. Giga-press cuts casting 22%, takt to 16 hours; cell-to-chassis +30%; SiC modules in-house -25% dependency. Energy down 28% to 1,200 kWh/vehicle. COGS to $28,500, margins +420 bps to 24.5%, EBITDA 15.2%. Q4 capex $1.1 billion, breakeven H1 2025.

We're confident in scaling further.

Following me, Elena Vasquez will provide insights into our technological advancements.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Mike. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to maintain our edge. Advancements in battery tech—like our LMFP and silicon anodes for higher density—and autonomous systems position us as EV leaders. FSD v12.3 neural nets, Dojo expansion, and V2X charging pilots are transforming our fleet. OTA success at 99.9%, trained on billions of miles, with robotaxi scaling ahead.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks. On the CyberVolt ramp, how sustainable is the 450% YoY growth given supply constraints, and what's the implied margin contribution?

Jordan Hale:
Great question. CyberVolt's growth is backed by Texas Giga ramping to 2,500 weekly, with 92% reservation conversion. Supply is solid via localized 4680s and Panasonic yields; margins are premium at 28% due to $125,000 ASPs and FSD bundles. We'll hit 60,000 in Q4 without issues.

Analyst 2:
Alex, can you elaborate on software guidance risks, especially regulatory in EU and China?

Alex Rivera:
Absolutely. Q3's $1.6-1.8 billion guide assumes 50% growth, but EU AI Act and China data rules are hurdles—we're mitigating with geo-fenced rollouts and Baidu ties. Retention at 95% and cash for Dojo keep us on track for 30% AV market share.

Analyst 3:
Mike, with expansions, how are you addressing labor and semi shortages in Europe and Texas?

Mike Thornton:
We're ahead: AI predictive maintenance cuts labor needs 20%, and 98% localization targets mitigate semis via TSMC allocations. Europe grants cover Brandenburg hires; Texas at full utilization by Q1.

Analyst 4:
Elena, on battery trends, when do we see solid-state in production, and impact on range/costs?

Elena Vasquez:
Pilots start Q2 2025 with QuantumScape JV, targeting 800 Wh/kg and $50/kWh—400-mile packs routine. Roadmap integrates with 2026 vehicles for 20% cost cuts, 1,000+ cycles.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Analyst 5:
Jordan, strategic outlook for emerging markets like India—any updates on JVs and volume targets?

Jordan Hale:
India JV with Tata breaks ground Q1 2025 for 200k capacity; targeting 5% share in sub-$25k segment with LFP Compact. APAC ex-China up 42% this quarter; scaling to 15% of volume by 2027.

Analyst 6:
Alex, overall FY24 revenue now at $10.5-11 billion earlier—has Q3 changed that, and 2025 EPS path?

Alex Rivera:
Q3 strength lifts FY24 to $55-57 billion total, +35% YoY. 2025 $18-20 billion revenue, 12-15% EBITDA margins, 25-30% EPS growth via scale and software.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead—from CyberVolt scaling and robotaxi revenue to battery deflation and global expansion—and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
